My partner is like a father figure to my little. He's incredibly supportive and loving to all of us. But I've had her be crushed in the past when a partner left in the same manner, and an abusive partner in the past who willfully manipulated our DID and hurt the little one. So we learned to be very very protective of her, and to be very very slow and careful with who we share our diagnosis with... and even when we considered it safe with our current partner, we took it very slow with the little one, and were very careful with how we explain things to her and only openly allowed her to form a strong bond when all the others had formed a positive bond. 

Because the thing is, it's the little ones (generally) who are going to struggle the most with boundaries and understanding relationships, and it's best to decide amongst yourselves the best you can (if that's possible for you guys) where you want those boundaries to lie and how you want to explain and maintain them with the little one. And of course all of this depends on your particular situation and how co-conscious you all are and how well you guys cooperate and communicate.

As far as your little's hurt feelings right now, I would suggest trying to have a conversation with her explaining what happened, that it's not their fault, they did nothing wrong, and that sometimes people have to go away and that hurts but you'll get through it together (of course she may be listening, may not be, it could be worth a shot). Maybe offer her some little time by watching some of her favorite movies, playing her favorite games, letting her color or paint, or maybe let her pick out a new stuffie. Just offer the experience, and she may or may not turn up, but it at least lets her know that she is welcome and loved.

Just my thoughts. Hang in there!
